Huntley College of Agriculture College of Business Administration College of Education and Integrative Studies College of Engineering College of Environmental Design College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences College of Science The Collins College of Hospitality Management College of Professional and Global Education University Library Student Programs for Support and Enrichment Centers and Institutes University Interdisciplinary Programs Index of Courses Index of Academic Programs Index of Roadmaps Index of Academic Colleges, Departments, and Programs University Administration, Regulations, and History Directory Archived Catalog PDFs My Portfolio Add to My Favorites (opens a new window) Share this Page Facebook this Page (opens a new window) Tweet this Page (opens a new window) Print (opens a new window) Help (opens a new window) 2026-2027 University Catalog Plant Science Department Building 2 Room 114 | (909) 869-2214 | Department Website | Faculty Directory The Department’s mission is to fully prepare students with the skill set that is required for career success in plant-based agriculture in the 21st century. The department embodies Cal Poly Pomona’s polytechnic values through a curriculum grounded in sustainability, ethical land stewardship, and applied agricultural science. Faculty actively mentor students across diverse fields, including horticulture, agronomy, pest management, urban agriculture, and soil science. Courses incorporate sustainability science and social responsibility, with required coursework in ethics and sustainability. Department culture is defined by interdisciplinary collaboration, inclusive teaching, and a commitment to advancing equity and environmental justice. Research and instruction are supported by faculty expertise in controlled-environment agriculture, hydroponics, agroecology, and beekeeping. Students engage in hands-on learning across 150 acres of farmland at Spadra Farm, 46,000 square feet of greenhouse space, a certified organic micro-farm, on-campus crop plots, and the department-managed apiary. The Center for Turfgrass, Irrigation, and Landscape Technology (CTILT) supports student research and training in landscape management, climate-smart plant selection, and water conservation. Students participate in national intercollegiate competitions in crops, soils, irrigation, and entomology, and hold internships with growers, landscape firms, and irrigation consulting companies. courses.title: Orientation to Plant Science
courses.description: Outline the academic path that students will follow to be successful in this major. Discuss the various employment opportunities available for students graduating with this degree. Course is for first quarter freshmen. Course is for first quarter freshmen.

courses.title: Seeds to Systems: The Biology of Plants and Agriculture
courses.description: Introduction to the biological principles and scientific methods that form the foundation of modern agriculture. Examination of how plants grow, develop, and interact with their environment, exploring topics such as crop production, genetics, and sustainable farming practices. Through inquiry-based learning and data analysis, topics connect plant science to real-world agricultural challenges-including food security, climate resilience, and resource conservation-while highlighting ethical, cultural, and technological perspectives in the field.

courses.title: Horticulture and Greenhouse Management
courses.description: Explore the fascinating world of plants and the intricate processes governing their growth, development, and interactions with the environment. An introduction to Plant Science that provides a comprehensive understanding of the biological, chemical, and physical principles that support plant life and cultivation. Emphasis is placed on plant anatomy, physiology, reproduction, taxonomy, soil science, and sustainable production practices. Gain a foundation for advanced studies in plant science, horticulture, and sustainable agriculture. Corequisite(s): PLT 1120L .

courses.title: Horticulture and Greenhouse Management
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental principles and practices of horticulture in landscape, greenhouse, and controlled environment systems. Emphasis on plant identification, anatomy, and physiology, along with applied skills in propagation, pruning, soils, irrigation, hydroponics, pest management, turfgrass, and nursery/greenhouse operations. Gain hands-on experience through laboratory and field activities designed to prepare for careers in horticulture and plant science. Corequisite(s): PLT 1120 .

courses.title: Agronomy and Farm Management
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of crop production and management, exploring environmental and economic factors that shape agriculture. Delve into crop biology, soil health, and pest management, with a strong focus on sustainable practices and innovations. Highlighting modern techniques like precision agriculture and biotechnology to address critical challenges such as climate change and global food security. Corequisite(s): PLT 1130L .

courses.title: Agronomy and Farm Management Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experiences that complement the lecture component. Engage in practical activities related to crop production, soil health, and pest management. Through experiments and fieldwork, develop essential skills in crop assessment and sustainable practices, applying scientific principles to real-world agricultural challenges. Corequisite(s): PLT 1130 .

courses.title: The Living Landscape
courses.description: Experiential and field-based instruction introduces plant identification and ecological/agricultural observation through weekly guided walks at Cal Poly Pomona. Exploring the university’s diverse landscapes-including natural hillsides, restored habitats, designed gardens, and active crop fields-practice includes recognizing plant traits, understanding ecological relationships, and considering agricultural and cultural uses of plants. Emphasis placed on field notebook skills, plant and insect identification, seasonal changes, and connections between natural and managed systems.

courses.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Subtropical Fruits
courses.description: Production of sub-tropical fruits and crops. Propagation, problem solving, harvesting, selection of best varieties and post-harvest technologies. Corequisite(s): PLT 2020L .

courses.title: Subtropical Fruits Laboratory
courses.description: Subtropical fruits, including date, olive, fig, macadamia, and other selected fruits for commercial planting. Climatic and cultural requirements, fruiting and growth habits, varietal characteristics. Corequisite(s): PLT 2020 .

courses.title: History of Garden Art
courses.description: [GE 3A] The relationship of ornamental flora to the human living experience to show the continuity with contemporary gardens, homes, parks and other art. An introduction to the various styles in landscape art as they developed in different cultures and in preceding ages.

courses.title: Agronomic Principles and Practices Laboratory
courses.description: Production and management of major agronomic crops in California such as cereals, field beans, sugar beets, corn and potatoes. Characteristics of major varieties in relation to applicable cultural practices, cost of production, harvesting, marketing, grading and processing. Corequisite(s): PLT 2200 .

courses.title: Culinary Produce Technology
courses.description: An integration of principles of culture, procurement, identification, and quality of both standard and gourmet vegetables, fruits, and herbs for restaurant and culinary uses. On site studies/discussion. Organic vs. standard produce. Case studies.

courses.title: Forage and Pasture Crops
courses.description: Establishment, management, and composition of irrigated and rangeland pastures adapted to southwestern conditions. Identification, botanical characteristics, and livestock utilization of major pasture species. Corequisite(s): PLT 2230L .

courses.title: Forage and Pasture Crops Laboratory
courses.description: Establishment, management, and composition of irrigated and rangeland pastures adapted to southwestern conditions. Identification, botanical characteristics, and livestock utilization of major pasture species. Corequisite(s): PLT 2230 .

courses.title: Vegetable Crop Systems
courses.description: Cultural practices, varieties, economics of production of major warm and cool season vegetables. Application of production techniques on college operated acreage. Corequisite(s): PLT 2260L .

courses.title: Vegetable Crop Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Cultural practices, varieties, economics of production of major warm and cool season vegetables. Application of production techniques on college operated acreage, including Spadra farm. Corequisite(s): PLT 2260 .

courses.title: Introduction to Soil Science
courses.description: A comprehensive overview of the fundamental concepts and principles of soil science, emphasizing the critical role soils play in ecosystems, agriculture, and environmental sustainability. Explore the formation, classification, and properties of soils, including physical, chemical, and biological aspects. Topics will cover soil ecology, nutrient management, soil conservation practices, and the impact of human activities on soil health. Corequisite(s): PLT 2310L .
courses.prerequisites: CHM 1210 and CHM 1210L .

courses.title: Introduction to Soil Science Laboratory
courses.description: Essential techniques for analyzing soil properties, including texture, structure, pH, moisture content, and nutrient composition. Through guided laboratory exercises, they will develop skills in soil sampling, testing methods, and data interpretation, fostering a deeper understanding of soil and management practices. Corequisite(s): PLT 2310 .
courses.prerequisites: CHM 1210 and CHM 1210L .

courses.title: Basic Irrigation Science
courses.description: An introduction to irrigation methods, such as drip, micro, surface and sprinkler for nursery, landscape, runoff, field crops and tree plant crop irrigations. Basic soil-plant-water relationships. Information needed for planning, designing, and scheduling of an irrigation system, irrigation hydraulics, irrigation efficiencies, and modern controllers.

courses.title: Introduction to Arthropods
courses.description: Arthropods and certain relatives affecting food, plants, animals, people, and their structures. Emphasizing insects, mites, ticks, spiders, and miscellaneous related groups; their morphological and phylogenetic relationships; habits and habitats; important characteristics affecting the well-being of people. Corequisite(s): PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Introduction to Arthropods Laboratory
courses.description: Arthropods and certain relatives affecting food, plants, animals, people, and their structures. Emphasizing insects, mites, ticks, spiders, and miscellaneous related groups; their morphological and phylogenetic relationships; habits and habitats; important characteristics affecting the well-being of people. Corequisite(s): PLT 2330 .

courses.title: Introduction to Plant Morphology and Anatomy
courses.description: Exploration of plant form and function at multiple levels of organization, from cells and tissues to whole plants. Topics include plant anatomy, morphology, growth and development, and adaptations to the environment. Emphasis on connecting plant structure to ecological function and agricultural applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Turfgrass Management
courses.description: The grasses, materials, and techniques involved in the maintenance and management of all types of athletic and recreational fields. Corequisite(s): PLT 2400L .

courses.title: Introduction to Turfgrass Management Laboratory
courses.description: The grasses, materials, and techniques involved in the maintenance and management of all types of athletic and recreational fields. Corequisite(s): PLT 2400 .

courses.title: Plant Identification
courses.description: Study of plant identification through taxonomic, morphological, and ecological approaches. Emphasis on vegetative and reproductive structures, diagnostic traits, and classification of major plant families found in California. Develop observation and identification skills through fieldwork, laboratory practice, and applied exercises. Includes discussion of cultural and ecological perspectives on plant diversity, naming, and use. Corequisite(s): PLT 2420L .

courses.title: Plant Identification Laboratory
courses.description: Study of trees, shrubs, vines and groundcovers, and herbaceous plant materials which are of the greatest ornamental value in the California landscape. Approximately 200 types will be identified and described according to growth habit, cultural requirements and use in the landscape.

courses.title: Computer Aided Design
courses.description: Introduction to computer-aided drafting/design intended for irrigation system design and other horticultural applications. Basic CAD commands, tools, multi-view drawing and dimensioning techniques. Corequisite(s): PLT 2520L .

courses.title: Computer Aided Design Laboratory
courses.description: An introductory course in computer-aided drafting/ design intended for irrigation system design and other horticultural applications. Basic CAD commands, tools, multi-view drawing and dimensioning techniques. Corequisite(s): PLT 2520 .

courses.title: Farmers’ Markets
courses.description: A survey of the business, production, social and regulatory aspects of farmers’ markets. The logistics and marketing aspects of selling at farmers’ markets and managing farmers’ markets will be discussed along with the history of the modern farmers’ market and current trends.

courses.title: Insects and Civilization
courses.description: [GE 5D] Analysis of insects and related arthropods and their influence on life, ranging from everyday events to how they have changed the history of the world. Selected topics on the importance of arthropods in modern and ancient cultures. Course synthesizes biological and historical topics related to arthropods in context of major world events and cultures both past and present, fields of study including science and technology, medicine, world hunger relief, and others. Open to all majors. Open to all majors.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Veterinary Entomology
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to the study of arthropods of veterinary importance, emphasizing their biology, taxonomy, and impact on animal health and productivity. Topics include arthropod morphology and classification, the biology and control of parasitic insects and arachnids, and the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases affecting domestic and livestock species. Special attention is given to major groups such as lice, fleas, mites, flies, mosquitoes, and ticks, as well as to arthropod transmission of bacterial, protozoan, and viral pathogens. Topics cover integrated pest management strategies and diagnostic techniques used in veterinary practice for a a foundational understanding of veterinary entomology.

courses.title: Technology Innovations in Plant Science
courses.description: Introduction to new technologies and innovations in the Plant Science industry. Various guest lectures from industry and academic professionals.

courses.title: Pesticide Laws and Regulations
courses.description: Federal and California Laws and Regulations affecting individuals, corporations, and agencies providing for the public health, safety and welfare; and protecting the environment including our natural resources. Emphasis on hazardous materials, ground water protection, pesticides, and pest control laws and regulation. Pesticide safety included. Function and structure of pertinent federal, state and county agencies and their enforcement practices as they relate to agribusiness, public health and pest control operations, including case studies.

courses.title: Agricultural Insect Pests
courses.description: Recognition and distribution of important insects and mites attacking agricultural crops such as the major field, cereal and truck crops, and citrus, avocado, deciduous fruit, small fruit, berries, grapes, and nut trees. Host preference and identification of damage to plant parts, seasonal history, habits and problems relating to pest management programs. Corequisite(s): PLT 3200L .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 233 or PLT 2330 ; and PLT 233L or PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Agricultural Insect Pests Laboratory
courses.description: Recognition and distribution of important insects and mites attacking agricultural crops such as the major field, cereal and truck crops, and citrus, avocado, deciduous fruit, small fruit, berries, grapes, and nut trees. Host preference and identification of damage to plant parts, seasonal history, habits and problems relating to pest management programs. Corequisite(s): PLT 3200 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 233 or PLT 2330 ; and PLT 233L or PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Arboriculture
courses.description: The ecological significance of trees, urban forestry principles, and the role of arborists in promoting sustainable landscapes. Development of practical skills in assessing tree health and diagnosing common issues, while also understanding the legal and ethical considerations in arboriculture, through lectures, case studies, and hands-on activities. Corequisite(s): PLT 3280L .

courses.title: Arboriculture Laboratory
courses.description: Care and management of specimen ornamental trees. Cavity repairs, bracing and cabling, pruning. Practice in the use of lines and climbing. Safety practices. Corequisite(s): PLT 3280 .

courses.title: Weed Science
courses.description: Recognition and control of weeds occurring in crop and range lands, ornamental plantings, and non-cropped situations. Classification of weeds. Cultural, chemical, and biological control practices. Laws and regulations. Corequisite(s): PLT 3310L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 115 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 115L or BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Weed Science Laboratory
courses.description: Recognition and control of weeds occuring in crop and rangelands, ornamental plantings, and non-cropped situations. Classification of weeds. Cultural, chemical and biological control practices. Laws and regulations. Corequisite(s): PLT 3310 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 115 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 115L or BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Soil Fertility and Fertilizers
courses.description: Examine soil nutrient availability, the impact of fertilizers on plant mineral nutrition and crop production, and the interpretation of soil test results for fertilization decisions. Addresses the economic and environmental implications of fertilizer use, emphasizing sustainable practices and the role of precision agriculture in enhancing nutrient use efficiency. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): PLT 3320LW .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 2310 , PLT 2310L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Bee Science
courses.description: Care, management, and manipulation of bees. Practical application of principles for effective establishment and maintenance of apiaries. Pollination and value of bees to agriculture. Recognition and control of bee diseases. Recognition and importance of native, commercial and introduced plants as nectar and pollen sources. Corequisite(s): PLT 3360L .

courses.title: Bee Science Laboratory
courses.description: Care, management, and manipulation of bees. Practical application of principles for effective establishment and maintenance of apiaries. Pollination and value of bees to agriculture. Recognition and control of bee diseases. Recognition and importance of native, commercial and introduced plants as nectar and pollen sources. Corequisite(s): PLT 3360 .

courses.title: Native Plant Materials
courses.description: Native California plant materials suitable for landscape purposes. Their identification, habits of growth, cultural requirements and landscape use. Corequisite(s): PLT 3370L .

courses.title: Native Plant Materials Laboratory
courses.description: Native California plant materials suitable for landscape purposes. Their identification, habits of growth, cultural requirements and landscape use. Corequisite(s): PLT 3370 .

courses.title: Sprinkler/Drip Irrigation
courses.description: An introduction to sprinkler and drip micro-irrigation systems and techniques. Systems will be discussed that apply to landscape and agronomic crops. Water savings and management will be a major part of this course.

courses.title: Professional Development and Leadership in Plant Science
courses.description: Provides foundational career readiness for plant science students. Professionalizing projects include building professional documents (resume, cover letter, personal statement), practicing interviewing and networking skills, and exploring diverse career pathways through guest speakers and applied activities. Emphasis is placed on leadership identity, communication, and professional preparation. Culmination of course incorporates a professional showcase with portfolio presentations to demonstrate career readiness. Focuses on early-stage professional development.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing.

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650L .

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture Laboratory
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650 .

courses.title: Urban and Community Agriculture
courses.description: [GE 5D] An integration of production methods and technology, social enterprise, and emerging business models for urban agriculture. Emphasis on growing, distributing, and marketing food and other products within metropolitan areas. Topics include community and school gardens, backyard plots, rooftop gardens, aquaponics, hydroponics, vertical farming and more. Attention to community development components of urban agriculture. Lecture, discussion, urban farm case studies and guest speakers with an emphasis on Southern California.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Farm-to-Table
courses.description: Cross Listed as: NTR 3860 Study of the farm-to-table movement. Focus in this course will be on small scale production, farmer’s markets and utilization of farm products. For nutrition, plant science, hospitality, and food science majors as well as plant-based nutrition and urban agriculture minors.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Crop Ecology
courses.description: Group research and writing project integrating environmental, ecological, economic, pest and disease management, genetics, and soil and water management in a business management setting.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and PLT 231L or PLT 2310L .

courses.title: Viticulture
courses.description: An examination of the cultural practices of worldwide, national and California grape growing systems in relation to wine and table grapes. Areas of discussion will include the climatic and cultural requirements, growth and fruiting habits, and varietal characteristics of fruit bearing plants. The production and maintenance of vineyard crops will include applicable cultural practices, site selection, variety selection, irrigation, pest management, harvesting and processing. Corequisite(s): PLT 4030L .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 131 or PLT 1120 ; and PLT 131L or PLT 1120L .

courses.title: Viticulture Laboratory
courses.description: Hands on experience of the cultural practices of grape growing systems in relation to wine and table grapes, growth and fruiting habits, and varietal characteristics of fruit bearing plants. The laboratory activities will include establishment and maintenance of vineyard crops and will include applicable cultural practices, site selection, variety selection, irrigation, pest management, harvesting and processing. Corequisite(s): PLT 4030 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 131 or PLT 1120 ; and PLT 131L or PLT 1120L .

courses.title: Plant Breeding
courses.description: Principles and technology used to improve crop plants. Genetic principles, principles of application, application of biotechnology, and breeding methods. Field plot design and statistics used in plant breeding programs. Corequisite(s): PLT 4040L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 115 or BIO 1150 ; and BIO 115L or BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Plant Breeding Laboratory
courses.description: Principles and technology used to improve crop plants. Genetic principles, principles of application, application of biotechnology, and breeding methods. Field plot design and statistics used in plant breeding programs. Corequisite(s): PLT 4040 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 115 or BIO 1150 ; and PLT 115L or BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Environmental Toxicology
courses.description: Survey and analyses of the effects of civilization on the environment. Emphasis will be placed on the effects of agriculture and other forms of commerce on food, water, air, soil, and human health.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and PLT 231L or PLT 2310L .

courses.title: Landscape Contracting and Estimating
courses.description: Management of landscape contracting firms. Bonding, insurance, contracts, ownership, licensing and other legal aspects of improvement to real property. Calculation of costs, manpower, and quantities of materials in landscape development. Preparation of specifications and estimates used in bidding. Corequisite(s): PLT 4160L .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 131 or PLT 1120 ; and PLT 131L or PLT 1120L .

courses.title: Landscape Contracting and Estimating Laboratory
courses.description: Calculation of cists, manpower and quantities of materials in landscape development. Preparation of specificationa and estimates used in bidding. Corequisite(s): PLT 4160 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 131 or PLT 1120 ; and PLT 131L or PLT 1120L .

courses.title: Plant Pathology
courses.description: Basic introduction to Plant Pathology, the organisms that cause plant disease and the conditions that provide the proper environment for disease to occur. Biotic and abiotic disease will be covered. Corequisite(s): PLT 4190L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201 or BIO 2050 ; and BOT 201L or BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plant Pathology Laboratory
courses.description: Plant pathology lab and field methodologies for isolation and diagnosis of plant disease. Corequisite(s): PLT 4190 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201 or BIO 2050 ; and BOT 201L or BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Production Mycology
courses.description: An advanced exploration of indoor mushroom cultivation with a focus on sustainable production systems, biotechnology, and entrepreneurship. Study of fungal biology, substrate science, climate control, spawn technologies, food safety, and emerging applications such as mycoremediation and mycomaterials. Emphasis on critical thinking, applied problem-solving, and industry readiness for careers in controlled environment agriculture. Corequisite(s): PLT 4210L .

courses.title: Production Mycology Laboratory
courses.description: Engage in hands-on mushroom production using a fully equipped indoor facility with IoT monitoring systems. Topics include sterile culture, substrate preparation, inoculation, spawn management, environmental control, harvesting, packaging, and entrepreneurship projects. Corequisite(s): PLT 4210 .

courses.title: Specialized Plant Propagation
courses.description: Current topics in plant propagation concerning juvenility, growth regulators, scion/rootstock combinations, and tissue culturing. Emphasis on commercial propagation by cuttings, grafting/budding, tissue culturing, division, layering, and seeding. Corequisite(s): PLT 4220L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 428 or BIO 4480 ; and BOT 428L or BIO 4480L .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 6 units.

courses.title: Specialized Plant Propagation Laboratory
courses.description: Current topics in plant propagation concerning juvenility, growth regulators,scion/rootstock combinations, and tissue culturing. Emphasis on commercial propagation by cuttings, grafting/budding, tissue culturing, division, layering, and seeding. May be repeated up to three times for a total credit of 3 units. Corequisite(s): PLT 4220 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 428 or BIO 4480 ; and BOT 428L or BIO 4480L .

courses.title: Applied Plant Physiology
courses.description: Study of plant physiological processes, including water relations, soil interactions, mineral nutrition, and responses to abiotic and biotic stressors, with an emphasis on practical applications in agriculture and natural ecosystems.

courses.title: Soil Chemistry
courses.description: Examines the fundamental chemical principles governing reactions in soils, with emphasis on soil mineralogy, surface chemistry, soil carbon transformations, and redox processes. Topics will focus on the theoretical basis of modern analytical and spectroscopic techniques used to study soil chemical processes.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 2310 and PLT 2310L .

courses.title: Soil Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Critical evaluation of the basic concepts and scientific methodologies regarding the chemical composition and reactions of the integrated solid productivity and environmental quality as influenced by social, political, and economic institution inwestern and non-western societies. Corequisite(s): PLT 4310 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and PLT 231L or PLT 2310L .

courses.title: Plants and Civilization
courses.description: [GE 5D] A critical review of science, technology and environment as related to plant domestication and current world food, fiber, and fuel production. Societal implications associated with the biological and technical innovations in world cropping systems will be discussed. Open to all majors. Open to all majors.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Golf Course Management
courses.description: The management, supervision, maintenance and operation of golf courses. A study of the equipment, scheduling, promotion and personnel required and related facilities of public and private courses. Corequisite(s): PLT 4340L .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 240 or PLT 2400 ; and PLT 240L or PLT 2400L .

courses.title: Golf Course Management Laboratory
courses.description: The management, supervision, maintenance and operation of golf courses. A study of the equipment, scheduling, promotion and personnel required and related facilities of public and private courses. Corequisite(s): PLT 4340 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 240 or PLT 2400 ; and PLT 240L or PLT 2400L .

courses.title: Integrated Pest Management
courses.description: Concepts of pest management in agriculture, industrial, urban and structural situations. Pesticide categorization, toxicology, safety and formulation. Mechanical, physical, cultural and biological control in pest management systems.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 233 or PLT 2330 ; and PLT 233L or PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Advanced Beekeeping
courses.description: Building upon a foundational understanding of beekeeping and to deepen knowledge and skills in apiculture, advanced topics such as hive management, pest and disease control, bee breeding, and the ecological impact of beekeeping practices are covered. Manage a sustainable apiary, contribute to research, and promote bee health and conservation. Corequisite(s): PLT 4500L .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 3360 and PLT 3360L .

courses.title: Advanced Beekeeping Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on laboratory component complements PLT 4500. Practical experience in modern beekeeping techniques. Engage in activities such as hive inspections, disease diagnosis, and colony management strategies. Emphasis is placed on sustainable practices, honey extraction, and the use of innovative tools. Learn to assess bee behavior and environmental factors affecting hive health. Corequisite(s): PLT 4500 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 3360 and PLT 3360L .

courses.title: Geospatial Analysis of Soils, Plants, and People
courses.description: Exploration of mapping, GIS, and remote sensing can be applied to real-world problems in agriculture and the environment. Includes hands-on techniques for collecting, analyzing, and visualizing spatial data, with applications ranging from soils and nutrients to crops and ecosystems. Taught in three sections by faculty with expertise in soil science, ethnobotany, and precision agriculture, the course highlights how mapping tools support soil sampling, nutrient management, irrigation, adaptive farming, and environmental decision-making. Includes the implementation of practical skills in GIS, drone imaging, and remote sensing, preparing them to address challenges in sustainable agriculture and natural resource management.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: An analytica investigation of a Plant Science reearch project of special interest to the individual student, working under faculty supervision and culminating in a formal, rhetorical report. 160 hours minimum. May be taking up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Junior Standing.

courses.title: Senior Capstone Project
courses.description: Application of plant and soil science knowledge through a capstone experience. Students may complete an applied research project, collaborate with private industry or public agencies on real-world problems, or engage in professional fieldwork that integrates data collection, analysis, and communication related to plant science. Emphasis is placed on career development, problem-solving, and professional-level skills in plant science fields. Minimum 100 hours of project work required.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to three times with different topics for a total of 3 units.

courses.title: Apiary Capstone
courses.description: Hands-on activities, exploring the complete process of beekeeping and product creation using hive resources. Produce and market a variety of goods - such as candles, lip balm, salves, and honey - while designing packaging, running pop-up booths, and managing the course’s social media presence. Projects develop entrepreneurship, marketing, and sustainability skills while promoting honey bee health and environmental stewardship.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: 3 units

courses.title: Small-Scale Sustainable Farming
courses.description: The diverse components of agricultural production on a small scale. Examine a number of existing small scale production models. Critically analyze small-scale production systems to determine how well they achieve economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity. Corequisite(s): PLT 4965L .

courses.title: Small-Scale Sustainable Farming Laboratory
courses.description: Engage in practical activities covering soil health, composting, crop planning, and integrated pest management. Emphasizing sustainable techniques in small-scale farming, the course fosters teamwork and critical problem-solving skills, preparing students to apply sustainable practices in real-world settings. Corequisite(s): PLT 4965 .

courses.title: Urban Agriculture Policy and Community Development
courses.description: Explores the emerging urban agriculture movement and policy initiatives that promote farming in the city. Examination of existing laws and policies, impact on urban farming, and policy development and implementation, to develop skills in communicating with decision makers. Engagement in a practicum on a local urban agriculture policy issue. Includes guest speakers and field trips that highlight local urban farming and related policy development. Corequisite(s): PLT 4975L .

courses.title: Urban Agriculture Policy and Community Development Laboratory

courses.title: Urban Agriculture Business Models
courses.description: Introduction to the characteristics of urban agriculture business models and the knowledge required to start an economically sustainable urban agriculture business. Exploration of resources and support to urban farmers. Students develop a business plan focusing on existing or proposed urban agriculture enterprise.

courses.title: Plant Science Journal Club: AI Tools and Research Literacy
courses.description: Critical reading, analysis, and discussion of contemporary scientific literature in plant science, biotechnology, and sustainable agriculture. Integrates the use of AI-based research tools (such as semantic search engines, literature-summarizing models, and data-visualization platforms) to enhance comprehension and synthesis of scientific findings. Explore the responsible use of generative AI in literature review, idea formulation, and writing while developing professional communication and presentation skills essential for thesis or project work.

courses.description: Analysis and discussion of a selected topic in plant science based upon examination of the current literature, recent research advancements, and exposure to professional issues. Subject matter topic for course rotates. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 6 units.

Required for Advancement to Candidacy. May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 3 units.
